statement: Let Λ ∈ K and let Π be any countably infinite ICC group. Let ω, ν be arbitrary normalized scalar cocycles on them, and let t, s > 0. Then Lω(Λ)t ∼ = Lν(Π)s if and only if t = s and there are an isomorphism δ : Λ → Π and a normalized cochain b : Λ → T such that (1.1) ω(g, h) = b(g)b(h)b(gh)−1 ν(δ(g), δ(h)). Every specified isomorphism at unit scale has the form θ(ug) = w b(g)vδ(g)w∗ for a unitary w in the target. More explicitly, put M = Lω(Λ) and N = Lν(Π), and let θ : pMn(M)p −→ qMm(N)q be a specified isomorphism, where the unnormalized traces of p and q are t and s. Then t = s, and one may choose δ, b as above and z ∈ Mm,n(N) so that, for the canonical map φ(ug) = b(g)vδ(g), z∗ z = φ(n) (p), zz∗ = q, θ(x) = zφ(n) (x)z∗ . Whenever such an isomorphism exists, the recovered comparison group Π belongs to K . In particular every factor Lω(Λ) in this class has trivial fundamental group.
